sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1983. The historical relationships of the languages of Central Maluku, Indonesia (Pacific Linguistics D-47). Canberra: ANU. ix+168 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement of where Kaibobo stress falls. p.65: 'Kaibobo displays **e > e but **ə > e, when stressed, o when unstressed.[87] In words containing two occurrences of **ə the unstressed **ə > o by assimilation.' fn.88 p.145: 'unstressed **ə in Kaibobo regularly became e'. Presupposes word stress; p.65 and fn.88 give the conditioning in opposite directions. Explicit stress rules in the book concern only Hoamoal/Asilulu (pp.82-83), not Kaibobo.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (langsci 526).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kaibobo stress. pp.369-370 fn.1 re-analyses the Kaibobo *ə split as vowel-harmonic ('*ə > o /_(C)V[+back], *ə > e /_(C)V+front, *ə > e, o /_(C)#'), dropping Collins's stress conditioning. Appendix A.7 p.740 lists the only Kaibobo data sources as 'Collins 1983, van Ekris 1864, 1865'.
